notes: Wiring diagram image was not provided; connections are from the text: matrix powered from the Nano Matter 3.3V pin, controlled over I2C (SDA/SCL), plus GND. The photo shows a 4-wire Grove cable (red, black, white, yellow), modelled as 4 jumper wires.

Port names for arduino-nano-matter (3V3, A4, A5, GND, USB) and led-matrix-grove-8x8-rgb (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL) are assumed, since those catalogue entries were not shown. I2C on the Nano Matter is assumed to use A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL).
Breadboard hole positions for the Nano Matter pins and wire ends are assumed. The Nano is placed on the top bank with pins in row e, and each wire goes into row a of the same column strip.
The Nano Matter's other pins are not used by the circuit, so no edges are drawn for them.
The Eero Thread Border Router connects wirelessly (Thread/Matter), so it has no physical edge. The USB cable's far end (computer/power) is not part of the parts list.
The Alexa app and the Seeed_RGB_LED_Matrix library are software, so they are not nodes.
